mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day window are not statistically lower than during the previous 60-day window with similar FEDFUNDS path (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns within 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs month-over-month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: Over 50% of triggered periods show no statistically significant positive return (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3% followed by a sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates shifting demand-supply dynamics that produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 0.3% for two consecutive months and INDPRO < previous month's value
failure_condition: In > 70% of such events, the 5-day forward return is non-negative (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in the goods price index (not available in the provided catalog; fallback to GDPC1 as proxy for output) suggests supply-side weakness that depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: During supply shocks, 20-day forward returns remain flat or positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 4%, the discount rate for future cash flows is expected to decline, supporting higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Over 40% of such periods show no positive return (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (not directly observable; use PAYEMS as proxy for labor activity) coinciding with a rise in consumer confidence proxies (none available; use a placeholder) predicts positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 20,000 jobs in a single month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly higher than the prior 60-day window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (not available; use GDPC1 as proxy) and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) jointly predict a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as investor sentiment improves.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by > 2% while UNRATE decreases by > 0.1 percentage points
failure_condition: More than 60% of triggered events show non-positive returns (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 10% in three consecutive months indicates structural supply constraints, which typically precede negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 10% over three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns during such periods are not statistically lower than during a baseline period of normal production (p > 0.05).
